profiles.subject: Rust
profiles.scope: Rust Reference snapshot `c9cc32825b03fc206d9c6fe73e9ca6a2f3576d6c`. The edition-specific facet applies to Rust 2024.
profiles.identity_boundary: The language reference is the evidence for these scoped constructs. Compiler implementation strategies, Cargo conventions, and runtime behavior need separate sources.

facets.claim: An out-of-line module declaration loads its body from a file. In the absence of a path attribute, the lookup follows module paths and the documented naming and directory rules.
facets.limitation: The source distinguishes conventional module lookup from explicit path attributes. It does not establish package layout.

facets.claim: When control flow leaves a drop scope, associated variables drop in reverse declaration order and associated temporaries in reverse creation order.
facets.limitation: This applies within the drop scope. Edition, control flow, expression kind, and special scrutinee rules matter when determining a temporary's scope.

facets.claim: The reference marks extra temporary-scope narrowing for if let and block tail expressions in the 2024 edition.

profiles.subject: Kotlin
profiles.identity_boundary: These are Kotlin core-language claims. A shared JVM backend or Java library does not establish a Kotlin identity merge or identical Kotlin/Native, Kotlin/JS, and Kotlin/JVM behavior.

facets.claim: The specification distinguishes nullable and non-nullable type universes. A value of a non-nullable type cannot contain null under the described model.
facets.limitation: The claim concerns the type model. Interop flexible types and particular runtime null failures require separate treatment.

facets.claim: A class is closed when its declaration supplies neither open nor abstract. The source also explains the implicit abstract status of a sealed class.
facets.limitation: The rule concerns classes and includes the sealed-class qualification. Interface inheritance follows separate rules.

profiles.subject: Scala
profiles.scope: Scala 2.13 archived language specification, Classes and Objects. Source bytes are identified in the accession table.
profiles.identity_boundary: The claims concern Scala 2.13 language forms. Scala 3 and individual JVM compiler lowering require separately scoped sources.

facets.claim: The specification describes a lazy value as initialized on its first access.
facets.limitation: Recursive initialization may exhibit looping, and an exception has separate rules. The source does not imply eager initialization at declaration.

facets.claim: An object definition introduces a single object of a new class.
facets.limitation: This is the object-definition construct. An arbitrary class declaration or shared JVM runtime does not establish the same single-object behavior.

profiles.subject: Clojure
profiles.identity_boundary: Source-level descriptions from the Clojure/JVM distribution establish the identified API contract. ClojureScript or other implementations need their own sources.

facets.claim: The lazy-seq macro documents deferred realization through seq and caching of the resulting sequence.
facets.limitation: This is one Seqable value created by the macro. Evaluation of arbitrary applications is outside scope.

facets.claim: The swap! contract documents an atomic update derived from the current atom value and warns that the update function may be called more than once.
facets.limitation: The result concerns atom updates through this API. It supplies no exactly-once guarantee for the update function's side effects.

facets.claim: The ns macro sets the current namespace by an unevaluated name, creating it when needed, and supports optional namespace clauses.
facets.limitation: Compilation-only class generation follows separate behavior.

profiles.subject: PostgreSQL SQL dialect
profiles.scope: PostgreSQL 17.0 publisher-authored command reference source at `d7ec59a63d745ba74fba0e280bbf85dc6d1caa3e`.
profiles.identity_boundary: The source documents PostgreSQL commands at the named release. A generic SQL definition and the identity relationships of other dialects need their own governing evidence.

facets.claim: The optional INHERITS clause names parent tables whose columns are inherited when PostgreSQL defines the child. Its documented parent relationship is persistent.
facets.limitation: Type conflicts, declaration merging, and subsequent schema propagation have additional rules.

facets.claim: The optional PARTITION BY clause offers range, list, and hash strategies. List partitioning requires a single column or expression in the partition key.
facets.limitation: Range and hash have different key arity and operator-class constraints. The statement does not describe every data insertion outcome.

profiles.subject: SQLite SQL dialect
profiles.identity_boundary: The source supports claims about SQLite's parser at this release. It does not establish general SQL syntax or prove storage and constraint effects for executed databases.

facets.claim: For the parenthesized column-list form of CREATE TABLE, the parser accepts a table option set that can combine comma-separated options.
facets.limitation: The CREATE TABLE AS SELECT alternative is separately expressed in the grammar.

facets.claim: The parser recognizes WITHOUT ROWID and STRICT table options by case-insensitive name checks and maps them to different flags.
facets.limitation: The claim excludes downstream validation and storage behavior.

profiles.subject: Visual Basic for .NET
profiles.identity_boundary: This specification is scoped to Visual Basic for .NET. Retain classic Visual Basic 6 and Visual Basic for Applications as separate lineage investigations until exact historical crosswalks are reviewed. The .NET compilation rules do not transfer to either candidate.

facets.claim: Within the described compilation model, source files are processed together and their top-level declarations contribute to the implicit global namespace.
facets.locator: Source Files and Namespaces introduction, lines 1–25
facets.limitation: The source explicitly allows the compilation environment to override the implicit namespace.

facets.claim: An explicit Option Strict statement with no On or Off argument defaults to On. With no statement, the compilation environment selects the setting.
facets.limitation: The default for omitted statement is distinct from the default for an omitted argument.

facets.claim: An Imports directive makes names available to declarations in its source file. Its scope excludes other Imports statements and other source files.
facets.limitation: The source also describes implicit imports and separate import-name resolution rules.
